name_story.story: Haruna can be understood through the Arabic form هَارُون, whose central sense is haruna; aaron (prophet) (hausa form). Haruna is the Hausa form of Arabic هَارُون (Hārūn), the Quranic form of the prophet Aaron.

faq.a: Haruna is associated with the Arabic form هَارُون, whose core sense is haruna; aaron (prophet) (hausa form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Haruna?
faq.a: Haruna is associated with Arabic. Haruna is the Hausa form of Arabic هَارُون (Hārūn), the Quranic form of the prophet Aaron.
Yes — the underlying form هَارُون is Arabic.
Haruna can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Haruna should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Hārūn is the Quranic Arabic form of the prophet Aaron and occurs in the Quran.

faq.q: What does Haruna mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Haruna is rendered ہارون and carries the sense ہارون، نبی کا نام.

faq.q: What does Haruna mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Haruna is rendered هارون and carries the sense هارون، نام پیامبر.
A romanized syllable approximation is ha-ru-na. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Haruna?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Haruna, haruna. Script forms are هارون, هَارُون, ہارون, हारून.

faq.q: Is Haruna a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
